## Webb’s Journey from Deployment to Routine Science

The James Webb Space Telescope had to fold to fit inside the Ariane 5 rocket’s fairing. Unfolding it in space involved more than 50 major steps and over 300 possible single points of failure. Any one could have diminished or crippled the mission, and repair was not possible at Webb’s distance from Earth.

Deployment proceeded smoothly. By its second week, Webb’s secondary mirror and both primary-mirror wings had unfolded and latched, completing its operational configuration. But reaching that configuration was only one stage of the process.

Commissioning continued over the next several months. During the first month, the telescope and instruments cooled for several weeks. Mirror alignment took place in months two through four, followed by calibration of instrument modes in months five and six.

Webb began routine science operations after six months. Its timeline thus distinguishes reaching full deployment in the second week from completing commissioning and starting routine science.
